fixed_statement:
Keep the definitions of \(I,q,\Omega,A_\Omega,\EFill_f\), and \({\mathcal B}_z\).
Take measurable near-minimizers \(C_y^0\) with
\[
\Mass C_y^0\le2\EFill_f(y).
\]
Assume the averaged tightening estimate
\[
A_\Omega
\le C\left(R_1I+\frac{I^2}{S_1q}\right)
+\frac{C}{q}\int_Q\int_\Omega
\Mass(C_y^0\llcorner{\mathcal B}_z)\,dy\,dz .
\tag{EAT}
\]
Under \((\mathrm{EAT})\),
\[
A_\Omega\le C\left(R_1I+\frac{I^2}{S_1q}\right)
+C\frac{R_3R_4}{S_3S_4}A_\Omega .
\]
fixed_proof:
Standard measurable selection in the separable flat topology, or equivalently outer integration with \(\varepsilon\)-minimizers, is enough for this formal step.
Apply Proposition 7 to each \(C_y^0\) and integrate in \(y\):
\[
\frac1q\int_Q\int_\Omega
\Mass(C_y^0\llcorner{\mathcal B}_z)\,dy\,dz
\le C\frac{R_3R_4}{S_3S_4}\int_\Omega\Mass C_y^0\,dy.
\]
Using \(\Mass C_y^0\le2\EFill_f(y)\), the last integral is at most \(2A_\Omega\). Substitution into \((\mathrm{EAT})\) gives the stated inequality.
